t.1.48.12: Having heard the words of Viśvāmitra, Rāghava, together with Lakṣmaṇa, placing Viśvāmitra at the front, entered the hermitage.
t.1.48.11: Then come, O greatly radiant one, to the hermitage of that sage of meritorious deeds, and deliver this highly fortunate Ahalyā, who has the form of a goddess.
t.1.48.10: But from that time on, O Rāghava, Indra has borne the testicles of a ram, through the power of the great-souled Gautama and of his austerity.
t.1.48.13: And he beheld that greatly blessed woman, her splendour made radiant by austerity, hard to look upon even for the worlds, and for the suras and asuras, even when they drew near.
t.1.48.14: Her, fashioned with great effort by the Creator, divine and seemingly made of illusion, her limbs enveloped in smoke, like the radiance of the full moon veiled by mist.
t.1.48.9: From that time on, O Kākutstha, the assembled Pitṛdevas eat rams deprived of their testicles, for the gods had fitted Indra with the testicles of those rams.
t.1.48.15: She was like the radiance of the full moon veiled by frost and cloud, and, hard to approach, like the blazing radiance of the sun seen in the midst of the waters.
t.1.48.16: For by the word of Gautama she had become hard to behold for all three worlds, until the sight of Rāma.
t.1.48.8: Having heard the words of Agni, the assembled ancestral gods tore off the testicles of a ram and bestowed them upon the thousand-eyed one.
t.1.48.17: Then the two Rāghavas clasped her feet, and she, remembering the words of Gautama, received them both in turn.
t.1.48.18: With a well-composed mind she offered water for the feet, the respectful offering, and hospitality; and Kākutstha received them in the manner laid down by the sacred injunctions.
t.1.48.19: There was a great shower of flowers, accompanied by the sounds of the gods' kettledrums, and there was also a great assembly of Gandharvas and Apsarases.
t.1.48.20: Crying "Excellent, excellent!" the gods honored that Ahalyā, whose limbs had been purified by the power of her austerities and who was obedient to the will of Gautama.
t.1.48.21: Gautama too, of great splendour, joyful and united with Ahalyā, duly honoured Rāma, and then that great ascetic performed his austerities.
t.1.48.22: Rāma too, having duly received the highest honor from the great sage Gautama, then went on to Mithilā.
